meta.title: SEBI rules for listed entities and market intermediaries

instruments.title: The Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 (as amended by the Finance Act, 2021)
applies_to: Every intermediary associated with the securities market, listed companies, issuers and any person dealing in securities
key_concepts: Interim and final directions, including disgorgement (s. 11B)
Prohibition of manipulative and deceptive devices, insider trading and substantial acquisition (s. 12A)
Settlement of administrative and civil proceedings (s. 15JB)
Appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal (s. 15T)
core_obligations: s. 12(1): no stock broker, merchant banker, portfolio manager, investment adviser or other intermediary may buy, sell or deal in securities except under a certificate of registration from SEBI
s. 12A: no person may use manipulative or deceptive devices, deal on unpublished price sensitive information, or acquire control of a company except in line with SEBI regulations
s. 11(2A) and 11C: SEBI may call for information, inspect books and records, and investigate
timelines: s. 15T(3): appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal within 45 days of receiving the order
consequences_stated: s. 15A: failure to furnish information, returns or books, or furnishing false information: at least Rs 1 lakh, up to Rs 1 lakh a day while it continues, capped at Rs 1 crore
s. 15C: listed company or intermediary failing to redress investor grievances when called upon by SEBI: penalty under s. 15C
s. 15E: AMC breaching restrictions on its activities: at least Rs 1 lakh, up to Rs 1 lakh a day while it continues, capped at Rs 1 crore

s. 15EA: breach of the AIF, InvIT or REIT regulations or of SEBI directions: at least Rs 1 lakh, up to Rs 1 lakh a day while it continues, capped at Rs 1 crore or three times the gains made, whichever is higher
s. 15F: stock broker failing to issue contract notes or charging excess brokerage: penalty under s. 15F
s. 15G: insider trading: Rs 10 lakh up to Rs 25 crore or three times the profit, whichever is higher

s. 15H: failure to make takeover disclosures, a required public announcement or open offer, or to pay the offer consideration: Rs 10 lakh up to Rs 25 crore or three times the profit, whichever is higher
s. 15HA: fraudulent and unfair trade practices: Rs 5 lakh up to Rs 25 crore or three times the profit, whichever is higher
s. 15HB: breach with no separate penalty: Rs 1 lakh up to Rs 1 crore
s. 24(1): offence punishable with imprisonment up to 10 years, fine up to Rs 25 crore, or both
instruments.consequences_general: SEBI Act, 1992: SEBI may issue directions, including disgorgement and debarment (s. 11, 11B), pass cease and desist orders (s. 11D) and suspend or cancel registration (s. 12(3)). Adjudicating officers impose penalties under ss. 15A to 15HB: for example, failure to file returns or furnish information carries at least Rs 1 lakh, and up to Rs 1 lakh a day while it continues, capped at Rs 1 crore (s. 15A); insider trading and fraudulent or unfair trade practices carry Rs 10 lakh (s. 15G) or Rs 5 lakh (s. 15HA) up to Rs 25 crore or three times the profit, whichever is higher; any breach with no specific penalty carries Rs 1 lakh up to Rs 1 crore (s. 15HB). Contraventions are also offences punishable with imprisonment up to 10 years, a fine up to Rs 25 crore, or both (s. 24). Proceedings may be settled under s. 15JB. Appeals lie to the Securities Appellate Tribunal within 45 days (s. 15T).

instruments.title: SEBI (Settlement of Administrative and Civil Proceedings) Regulations, 2026
applies_to: Any person against whom proceedings under the SEBI Act, SCRA or Depositories Act have been or may be started
key_concepts: Settlement notice before a show cause notice
Settlement amount by formula: base amount, stage, gravity, aggravating and mitigating factors
Fast track settlement: violation based and monetary threshold based
Confidentiality and settlement with immunity for substantial assistance
Internal Committee, High Powered Advisory Committee and Panel of Whole Time Members
core_obligations: regulation 3(3): non-refundable application fee of Rs 25,000 for a natural person and Rs 35,000 for others
regulation 3(5): one application covering all proceedings on the same cause of action

regulation 6(1): not available where an application on the same default was rejected before, where an investigation is pending (except with confidentiality), or for wilful defaulters, fraudulent borrowers and fugitive economic offenders
regulation 6(2): defaults with market-wide impact, losses to many investors or harm to market integrity may not be settled
regulation 27: for delayed or wrong-format disclosures and delayed compliance, SEBI may issue a fast track settlement notice before starting proceedings
timelines: regulation 4(1): application within 90 days of the show cause notice (or supplementary notice), unless the matter is before the Tribunal or the Supreme Court
regulation 5(1): application within 60 days of receiving a settlement notice
regulation 3(7): a returned application may be refiled within 15 days
regulation 4(3) and (4): proceedings pending on 07-11-2026 that were not settled under the 2018 Regulations may be filed within 90 days, at a settlement amount 20% higher
consequences_stated: regulation 39: a settlement order may be revoked for breach of its terms or for lack of full and true disclosure; the proceedings are then restored and no amount is refunded

regulation 4(2): includes knowingly creating a false or misleading appearance of trading, manipulating prices, mis-selling of securities, services or mutual fund units, and publishing false or misleading information

instruments.title: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (last amended on 12-03-2025)
applies_to: Listed companies and companies proposing to list
Insiders, designated persons and their immediate relatives
Intermediaries and fiduciaries handling unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI)
key_concepts: Communication of UPSI only for legitimate purposes (regulation 3)
Trading while in possession of UPSI (regulation 4)
Disclosures by promoters, KMP, directors and designated persons (regulation 7)
Codes of conduct and fair disclosure (regulations 8, 9)
core_obligations: regulation 3: UPSI may be shared only for legitimate purposes, performance of duties or discharge of legal obligations
regulation 3(5): the board must ensure a structured digital database of persons with whom UPSI is shared
regulation 4(1): no insider may trade while in possession of UPSI, subject to the defences listed
regulation 5: a trading plan must be approved by the compliance officer and disclosed to the exchanges; the trade price may be capped at up to 20% above or below the closing price
regulation 9: listed companies and intermediaries must adopt a code of conduct for designated persons, including trading window and pre-clearance rules
Schedule B: the trading window closes from the end of every quarter until 48 hours after results are published
timelines: regulation 7(1)(b): a person appointed as KMP or director, or becoming a promoter or member of the promoter group, discloses holdings to the company within 7 days
regulation 7(2)(a): promoters, promoter group members, designated persons and directors disclose trades worth over Rs 10 lakh in a calendar quarter to the company within two trading days
regulation 7(2)(b): the company informs the stock exchanges within two trading days of receiving that disclosure
regulation 5(5): the compliance officer approves or rejects a trading plan within two trading days of receipt, and notifies an approved plan to the exchanges on the day of approval
regulation 5(2)(i): trading under the plan may start no earlier than 120 calendar days after its public disclosure
consequences_stated: SEBI Act s. 15G: Rs 10 lakh up to Rs 25 crore or three times the profit, whichever is higher
Schedule B: breach of the code of conduct is reported to SEBI and may lead to wage freeze, suspension or recovery

instruments.title: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (last amended on 15-10-2026)
applies_to: Every listed entity with specified securities (equity) listed on the main board, SME exchange or Innovators Growth Platform
Entities with listed non-convertible securities (Chapter V)

A high value debt listed entity (listed non-convertible debt of Rs 5,000 crore or more outstanding): regulations 15 to 27 apply under regulation 15(1A), and an entity with only listed debt follows Chapter VA (regulations 62B onwards)
key_concepts: Audit, nomination and remuneration, stakeholders relationship and risk management committees (regulations 18 to 21)
Related party transactions and materiality thresholds in Schedule XII (regulation 23)
Disclosure of material events (regulation 30 and Schedule III)
Obligations for listed non-convertible securities (Chapter V)
core_obligations: regulation 13(1): redress investor grievances within 21 calendar days of receipt, and stay registered on SCORES
regulation 17(2): the board meets at least four times a year, with no more than 120 days between meetings
regulation 21: the Risk Management Committee has at least three members and meets at least twice a year
regulation 23(1): a related party transaction is material if it crosses the Schedule XII thresholds; material transactions need prior shareholder approval
regulation 24A: the listed entity and its material unlisted Indian subsidiaries undergo secretarial audit by a peer reviewed company secretary
regulation 27(2): quarterly compliance report on corporate governance, signed by the compliance officer or CEO, including cyber security incidents
regulation 30: disclose material events; Para A of Schedule III events are deemed material, Para B events are tested against the materiality criteria
regulation 46: maintain a functional website with the required disclosures
timelines: regulation 30(6): board meeting outcomes within 30 minutes of the meeting closing (three hours if the meeting closes after market hours and more than three hours before the next session); events within the entity within 12 hours; other events within 24 hours, unless Schedule III sets another time
regulation 29: prior intimation of board meetings on specified matters at least two working days in advance
regulation 31(1)(b): shareholding pattern within 21 days of the end of each quarter (half-yearly for SME exchange)
regulation 33(3): quarterly results within 45 days of quarter end; annual audited results within 60 days of year end
regulation 52(1): debt listed entities file quarterly results within 45 days of quarter end (other than the last quarter)
regulation 57(1): certificate on payment of interest or principal on non-convertible securities within one working day of it falling due
regulation 15(1A) and 62C: an entity that crosses the Rs 5,000 crore high value debt threshold during the year complies within six months of the trigger
consequences_stated: Fines and freezing of promoter holdings by stock exchanges under the standard operating procedure in the LODR Master Circular
SEBI Act s. 15A(b), 15C and 15HB; SCRA s. 23E

core_obligations: regulation 6(1): an IPO issuer needs net tangible assets, operating profit, net worth and track record as listed, or must use the book building route with allotment mainly to qualified institutional buyers
regulation 14(1): promoters hold at least 20% of the post-issue capital, with permitted contributors able to meet a shortfall

timelines: regulation 16: lock-in of 18 months (or three years) for the minimum promoters' contribution

applies_to: Acquirers of shares, voting rights or control in a listed company, and persons acting in concert

key_concepts: Creeping acquisition of up to 5% a year (regulation 3(2))
core_obligations: regulation 3(1): no acquirer may acquire shares or voting rights which, with those of persons acting in concert, entitle them to 25% or more of the voting rights without a public announcement of an open offer
regulation 3(2): a holder of 25% or more but below the maximum non-public shareholding may not acquire more than 5% in a financial year without an open offer
regulation 4: acquiring control requires an open offer, whatever the shareholding
regulation 7(1): the open offer is for at least 26% of total shares
regulation 29(1) and (2): disclose holdings (with persons acting in concert) on reaching 5%, and every later acquisition or disposal that changes the holding by more than 2%
timelines: regulation 29(3): disclosures within two working days of the acquisition or disposal
consequences_stated: SEBI Act s. 15H: Rs 10 lakh up to Rs 25 crore or three times the profit, whichever is higher
regulation 32: directions, including divestment and making an open offer with interest

key_concepts: Board-approved buy-back up to 10% of paid-up capital and free reserves
Tender offer and open market routes
core_obligations: regulation 4(i): a buy-back may not exceed 25% of the aggregate paid-up capital and free reserves, on the standalone or consolidated financial statements, whichever is lower; equity shares bought back in a financial year may not exceed 25% of paid-up equity capital
regulation 5(i)(b): a buy-back needs a special resolution, except one of 10% or less of paid-up equity capital and free reserves, which the board may approve

applies_to: Listed companies and acquirers (promoters) seeking voluntary delisting of equity shares
Compulsory delisting by a stock exchange
key_concepts: Reverse book building and the discovered price
Success threshold of 90% of issued shares

Adjudicating officers impose penalties under ss. 15A to 15HB: for example, failure to file returns or furnish information carries at least Rs 1 lakh, and up to Rs 1 lakh a day while it continues, capped at Rs 1 crore (s. 15A); insider trading and fraudulent or unfair trade practices carry Rs 10 lakh (s. 15G) or Rs 5 lakh (s. 15HA) up to Rs 25 crore or three times the profit, whichever is higher; any breach with no specific penalty carries Rs 1 lakh up to Rs 1 crore (s. 15HB). Contraventions are also offences punishable with imprisonment up to 10 years, a fine up to Rs 25 crore, or both (s. 24). Proceedings may be settled under s. 15JB. Appeals lie to the Securities Appellate Tribunal within 45 days (s. 15T).

instruments.title: Master Circular for Online Resolution of Disputes in the Indian Securities Market
applies_to: Investors and clients, listed companies and SEBI-registered intermediaries, through the Smart ODR portal
key_concepts: Smart ODR portal run with the stock exchanges and depositories
core_obligations: Enrol on the ODR portal and take part in conciliation and arbitration of disputes with investors
Conciliation is concluded within 21 calendar days (extendable by 10 days with consent)
timelines: 21 calendar days for conciliation

instruments.title: Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF) for SEBI Regulated Entities, with clarifications of 2024-25
instruments.status: In force (with extended timelines in later circulars)
applies_to: SEBI regulated entities, graded by size: market infrastructure institutions, qualified, mid-size, small-size and self-certification entities, including AMCs, stock brokers, depository participants and AIFs
key_concepts: Governance, identify, protect, detect, respond and recover
Cyber Capability Index for MIIs and qualified entities
core_obligations: Adopt a board-approved cyber security and cyber resilience policy in line with the framework
Carry out VAPT at the frequency set for the entity's category
Report cyber incidents to SEBI and CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them
timelines: Cyber incidents reported within 6 hours
Adoption timelines were extended by the circulars of 28-03-2025 and 30-06-2025
